<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="113.39px"/><col width="501.71px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:20</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="161.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 19:16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TCP[3:0]</span>: Timestamp counter prescaler</p><p class="TableIndent">Configures the timestamp and timeout counters time unit in multiples of CAN bit times [1…16].</p><p class="TableIndent">The actual interpretation by the hardware of this value is such that one more than the value programmed here is used.</p><p class="TableIndent">In CAN FD mode, the internal timestamp counter TCP does not provide a constant time base due to the different CAN bit times between arbitration phase and data phase. Thus CAN FD requires an external counter for timestamp generation (TSS[1:0] = 10).</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield is write-protected (P): write access is possible only when the CCE and INIT bits of the FDCAN_CCCR register are both set.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="118.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 1:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TSS[1:0]</span>: Timestamp select</p><p class="TableIndent">00: Timestamp counter value always 0x0000</p><p class="TableIndent">01: Timestamp counter value incremented according to TCP</p><p class="TableIndent">10: External timestamp counter from TIM3 value (tim3_cnt[0:15])</p><p class="TableIndent">11: Same as 00.</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits are write-protected write (P): write access is possible only when the CCE and INIT bits of the FDCAN_CCCR register are both set.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 44.4.9 FDCAN timestamp counter value register (FDCAN\_TSCV)

Address offset: 0x0024

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="113.39px"/><col width="501.71px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="114.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TSC[15:0]</span>: Timestamp counter</p><p class="TableIndent">The internal/external timestamp counter value is captured on start of frame (both Rx and Tx). When TSS[1:0] = 01 in FDCAN_TSCC, the timestamp counter is incremented in multiples of CAN bit times [1 … 16] depending on the configuration of TCP[3:0] in FDCAN_TSCC. A wrap around sets the TSW interrupt flag in FDCAN_IR. Write access resets the counter to 0.</p><p class="TableIndent">When TSS[1:0] = 10, TSC[15:0] reflects the external timestamp counter value. A write access has no impact.</p></td></tr></table></div>


**Note:**

A “wrap around” is a change of the timestamp counter value from non-0 to 0 that is not caused by write access to FDCAN\_TSCV.

### 44.4.10 FDCAN timeout counter configuration register (FDCAN\_TOCC)

Address offset: 0x0028

Reset value: 0xFFFF 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="113.39px"/><col width="503.38px"/><tr height="70.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TOP[15:0]</span>: Timeout period</p><p class="TableIndent">Start value of the timeout counter (down-counter). Configures the timeout period.</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield is write-protected (P), write access is possible only when the CCE and INIT bits of the FDCAN_CCCR register are both set.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="193.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 2:1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TOS[1:0]</span>: Timeout select</p><p class="TableIndent">When operating in continuous mode, a write to FDCAN_TOCV presets the counter to the value configured by TOP[15:0] in FDCAN_TOCC and continues down-counting. When the timeout counter is controlled by one of the FIFOs, an empty FIFO presets the counter to the value configured by TOP[15:0]. Down-counting is started when the first FIFO element is stored.</p><p class="TableIndent">00: Continuous operation</p><p class="TableIndent">01: Timeout controlled by Tx event FIFO</p><p class="TableIndent">10: Timeout controlled by Rx FIFO 0</p><p class="TableIndent">11: Timeout controlled by Rx FIFO 1</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield is write-protected (P), write access is possible only when the CCE and INIT bits of the FDCAN_CCCR register are both set.</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ETOC</span>: Timeout counter enable</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Timeout counter disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Timeout counter enabled</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is write-protected (P), write access is possible only when the CCE and INIT bits of the FDCAN_CCCR register are both set.</p></td></tr></table></div>


For more details, see [Timeout counter](#XREF_56376__Timeout_counter30).

### 44.4.11 FDCAN timeout counter value register (FDCAN\_TOCV)

Address offset: 0x002C

Reset value: 0x0000 FFFF

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="113.39px"/><col width="502.54px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="84.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TOC[15:0]</span>: Timeout counter</p><p class="TableIndent">The timeout counter is decremented in multiples of CAN bit times [1 … 16] depending on the configuration of the TCP[3:0] bitfield of the FDCAN_TSCC register. When decremented to 0, the TOO interrupt flag is set in FDCAN_IR and the timeout counter is stopped. Start and reset/restart conditions are configured via TOS[1:0] in FDCAN_TOCC.</p></td></tr></table></div>

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="113.39px"/><col width="500.04px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:24</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="100.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 23:16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CEL[7:0]</span>: CAN error logging</p><p class="TableIndent">The counter is incremented each time when a CAN protocol error causes the transmit error counter or the receive error counter to be incremented. It is reset by read access to CEL[7:0]. The counter stops at 0xFF; the next increment of TEC[7:0] or REC[6:0] sets the ELO interrupt flag in FDCAN_IR.</p><p class="TableIndent">Access type is rc_r: cleared on read.</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 15</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RP</span>: Receive error passive</p><p class="TableIndent">0: The receive error counter is below the error passive level of 128.</p><p class="TableIndent">1: The receive error counter has reached the error passive level of 128.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 14:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL" style="font-weight:Bold;">REC[6:0]: <span style="font-weight:normal;">Receive error counter</span></p><p class="TableIndent">Actual state of the receive error counter, values between 0 and 127.</p></td></tr><tr height="85.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 7:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TEC[7:0]</span>: Transmit error counter</p><p class="TableIndent">Actual state of the transmit error counter, values between 0 and 255.</p><p class="TableIndent">When the ASM bit of the FDCAN_CCCR is set, the CAN protocol controller does not increment TEC and REC when a CAN protocol error is detected, but CEL[7:0] is still incremented.</p></td></tr></table></div>

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="113.39px"/><col width="501.71px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:23</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="84.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 22:16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TDCV[6:0]</span>: Transmitter delay compensation value</p><p class="TableIndent">Position of the secondary sample point, defined by the sum of the measured delay from FDCAN_TX to FDCAN_RX and TDCO[6:0] in FDCAN_TDCR. The SSP position is, in the data phase, the number of minimum time quanta (m<span style="font-size : 10.00pt;">t</span><sub><span style="font-size : 10.00pt;">q</span></sub>) between the start of the transmitted bit and the secondary sample point. Valid values are 0 to 127 × m<span style="font-size : 10.00pt;">t</span><sub><span style="font-size : 10.00pt;">q</span></sub>.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 15</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 14</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PXE</span>: Protocol exception event</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No protocol exception event occurred since last read access</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Protocol exception event occurred</p></td></tr><tr height="88.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 13</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">REDL</span>: Received FDCAN message</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set independent of acceptance filtering.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Since this bit was cleared by the CPU, no FDCAN message has been received.</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Message in FDCAN format with EDL flag set has been received.</p><p class="TableIndent">Access type is rc_r: cleared on read.</p></td></tr><tr height="88.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 12</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL" style="font-weight:Bold;">RBRS: <span style="font-weight:normal;">BRS flag of last received FDCAN message</span></p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set together with REDL, independent of acceptance filtering.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Last received FDCAN message did not have its BRS flag set.</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Last received FDCAN message had its BRS flag set.</p><p class="TableIndent">Access type is rc_r: cleared on read.</p></td></tr><tr height="88.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 11</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL" style="font-weight:Bold;">RESI<span style="font-weight:normal;">: ESI flag of last received FDCAN message</span></p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set together with REDL, independent of acceptance filtering.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Last received FDCAN message did not have its ESI flag set.</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Last received FDCAN message had its ESI flag set.</p><p class="TableIndent">Access type is rc_r: cleared on read.</p></td></tr><tr height="85.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 10:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DLEC[2:0]</span>: Data last error code</p><p class="TableIndent">Type of last error that occurred in the data phase of a FDCAN format frame with its BRS flag set. Coding is the same as for LEC[2:0]. This field is cleared when a FDCAN format frame with its BRS flag set has been transferred (reception or transmission) without error.</p><p class="TableIndent">Access type is rs: set on read.</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BO</span>: Bus-off status</p><p class="TableIndent">0: The FDCAN is not in bus-off state.</p><p class="TableIndent">1: The FDCAN is in bus-off state.</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 6</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">EW</span>: Warning status</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Both error counters are below the error-warning limit of 96.</p><p class="TableIndent">1: At least one of error counter has reached the error-warning limit of 96.</p></td></tr><tr height="70.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">EP</span>: Error passive</p><p class="TableIndent">0: The FDCAN is in the error-active state. It normally takes part in bus communication and sends an active error flag when an error has been detected.</p><p class="TableIndent">1: The FDCAN is in the error-passive state.</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 4:3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ACT</span><span class="Bold" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:Bold;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">[1:0]</span>: Activity</p><p class="TableIndent">Monitors the module’s CAN communication state.</p><p class="TableIndent">00: Synchronizing: node is synchronizing on CAN communication.</p><p class="TableIndent">01: Idle: node is neither receiver nor transmitter.</p><p class="TableIndent">10: Receiver: node is operating as receiver.</p><p class="TableIndent">11: Transmitter: node is operating as transmitter.</p></td></tr><tr height="389.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 2:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL" style="font-weight:Bold;">LEC[2:0]: <span style="font-weight:normal;">Last error code</span></p><p class="TableIndent">LEC[2:0] indicates the type of the last error to occur on the CAN bus. This bitfield is cleared when a message has been transferred (reception or transmission) without error.</p><p class="TableIndent">000: No error occurred since LEC[2:0] has been cleared by successful reception or transmission.</p><p class="TableIndent">001: Stuff error. More than five equal bits in a sequence have occurred in a part of a received message where this is not allowed.</p><p class="TableIndent">010: Form error. A fixed format part of a received frame has the wrong format.</p><p class="TableIndent">011: Ack error. The message transmitted by the FDCAN was not acknowledged by another node.</p><p class="TableIndent">100: Bit1 error. During the transmission of a message (with the exception of the arbitration field), the device wanted to send a recessive level (bit of logical value 1), but the monitored bus value was dominant.</p><p class="TableIndent">101: Bit0 error. During the transmission of a message (or acknowledge bit, or active error flag, or overload flag), the device wanted to send a dominant level (data or identifier bit logical value 0), but the monitored bus value was recessive. During bus-off recovery this status is set each time a sequence of 11 recessive bits has been monitored. This enables the CPU to monitor the proceeding of the bus-off recovery sequence (indicating the bus is not stuck at dominant or continuously disturbed).</p><p class="TableIndent">110: CRC error. The CRC check sum of a received message was incorrect. The CRC of an incoming message does not match with the CRC calculated from the received data.</p><p class="TableIndent">111: No change. Any read access to the protocol status register reinitializes LEC[2:0] to 7. When the LEC[2:0] shows the value 7, no CAN bus event was detected since the last CPU read access to the protocol status register.</p><p class="TableIndent">Access type is rs: set on read.</p></td></tr></table></div>


**Note:**

When a frame in FDCAN format has reached the data phase with the BRS flag set, the next CAN event (error or valid frame) is shown in DLEC[2:0] instead of LEC[2:0]. An error in a fixed stuff bit of an FDCAN CRC sequence is shown as a form error, not as a stuff error.

The bus-off recovery sequence (see CAN Specification Rev. 2.0 or ISO11898-1) cannot be shortened by setting or clearing the INIT bit of the FDCAN\_CCCR register. If the device enters bus-off, it sets the INIT bit of its own, stopping all bus activities. Once INIT has been cleared by the CPU, the device waits for 129 occurrences of bus-idle (129 × 11 consecutive recessive bits) before resuming normal operation. At the end of the bus-off recovery sequence, the error management counters are reset. During the waiting time after clearing INIT, each time a sequence of 11 recessive bits has been monitored, a bit0 error code is written to LEC[2:0] of FDCAN\_PSR, enabling the CPU to check up whether the CAN bus is stuck at dominant or continuously disturbed, and to monitor the bus-off recovery sequence. The REC[6:0] bitfield of the FDCAN\_ECR register is used to count these sequences.

### 44.4.14 FDCAN transmitter delay compensation register (FDCAN\_TDCR)

Address offset: 0x0048

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="113.39px"/><col width="500.04px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:15</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="85.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 14:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TDCO[6:0]</span>: Transmitter delay compensation offset</p><p class="TableIndent">Offset value defining the distance between the measured delay from FDCAN_TX to FDCAN_RX and the secondary sample point. Valid values are 0 to 127 × m<span style="font-size : 10.00pt;">t</span><sub><span style="font-size : 10.00pt;">q</span></sub>.</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield is write-protected (P), which means that write access is possible only when the CCE and INIT bits of the FDCAN_CCCR register are both set.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="85.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 6:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TDCF[6:0]</span>: Transmitter delay compensation filter window length</p><p class="TableIndent">Defines the minimum value for the SSP position, dominant edges on FDCAN_RX that would result in an earlier SSP position are ignored for transmitter delay measurements.</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield is write-protected (P), which means that write access is possible only when the CCE and INIT bits of the FDCAN_CCCR register are both set.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 44.4.15 FDCAN interrupt register (FDCAN\_IR)

The flags are set when one of the listed conditions is detected (edge-sensitive). The flags remain set until the host clears them. A flag is cleared by writing 1 to the corresponding bit position.

Writing 0 has no effect. A hard reset clears the register. The configuration of FDCAN\_IE controls whether an interrupt is generated. The configuration of FDCAN\_ILS controls on which interrupt line an interrupt is signaled.

Address offset: 0x0050

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="113.39px"/><col width="501.71px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:24</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 23</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ARA</span>: Access to reserved address</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No access to reserved address occurred</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Access to reserved address occurred</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 22</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PED</span>: Protocol error in data phase (data bit time is used)</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No protocol error in data phase</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Protocol error in data phase detected (DLEC[2:0] different from 0 and 7 in FDCAN_PSR)</p></td></tr><tr height="70.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 21</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PEA</span>: Protocol error in arbitration phase (nominal bit time is used)</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No protocol error in arbitration phase</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Protocol error in arbitration phase detected (LEC[2:0] different from 0 and 7 in FDCAN_PSR)</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 20</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">WDI</span>: Watchdog interrupt</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No message RAM watchdog event occurred</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Message RAM watchdog event due to missing READY</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 19</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BO</span>: Bus-off status</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Bus-off status unchanged</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Bus-off status changed</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 18</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">EW</span>: Warning status</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Error-warning status unchanged</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Error-warning status changed</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 17</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">EP</span>: Error passive</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Error-passive status unchanged</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Error-passive status changed</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ELO</span>: Error logging overflow</p><p class="TableIndent">0: CAN error logging counter did not overflow.</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Overflow of CAN error logging counter occurred.</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 15</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TOO</span>: Timeout occurred</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No timeout</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Timeout reached</p></td></tr><tr height="270.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 14</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">MRAF</span>: Message RAM access failure</p><p class="TableIndent">The flag is set when the Rx handler:</p><p class="RegTBullet2" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">-<span style="padding-right:10pt ;">​</span>has not completed acceptance filtering or storage of an accepted message until the arbitration field of the following message has been received. In this case acceptance filtering or message storage is aborted and the Rx handler starts processing of the following message. </p><p class="RegTBullet2" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">-<span style="padding-right:10pt ;">​</span>was unable to write a message to the message RAM. In this case message storage is aborted.</p><p class="TableIndent">In both cases the FIFO put index is not updated. The partly stored message is overwritten when the next message is stored to this location.</p><p class="TableIndent">The flag is also set when the Tx handler was not able to read a message from the message RAM in time. In this case message transmission is aborted. In case of a Tx handler access failure, the FDCAN is switched into restricted operation mode (see <a href="#XREF_70108__Restricted_Operation_Mode30" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Restricted operation mode</a>). To leave restricted operation mode, the host CPU has to clear the ASM of the FDCAN_CCCR register.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No message RAM access failure occurred</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Message RAM access failure occurred</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 13</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TSW</span>: Timestamp event FIFO element lost</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 11</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TEFF</span>: Tx event FIFO full</p><p element.</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 9</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TFE</span>: Tx FIFO empty </p><p class="TableIndent">0: Tx ### 44.4.16 FDCAN interrupt enable register (FDCAN\_IE)

The settings in the interrupt enable register determine which status changes in the interrupt register are signaled on an interrupt line.

Address offset: 0x0054

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RF0LE</span>: Rx FIFO 0 message lost interrupt enable</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Interrupt disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Interrupt enabled</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RF0NE</span>: Rx FIFO 0 new message interrupt enable</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Interrupt disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Interrupt enabled</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 44.4.17 FDCAN interrupt line select register (FDCAN\_ILS)

This register assigns an interrupt generated by a specific group of interrupt flags from the interrupt register to one of the two module interrupt lines. For interrupt generation, the respective interrupt line has to be enabled via the EINT0 and EINT1 bit of the FDCAN\_ILE register.

Address offset: 0x0058

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

### 44.4.18 FDCAN interrupt line enable register (FDCAN\_ILE)

Each of the two interrupt lines to the CPU can be enabled/disabled separately by programming the EINT0 and EINT1 bits.

Address offset: 0x005C

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

### 44.4.19 FDCAN global filter configuration register (FDCAN\_RXGFC)

Global settings for message ID filtering. The global filter configuration controls the filter path for standard and extended messages as described in [Figure 671](#XREF_62820__Figure_7__Standard_Message_ID_filter_path30) and [Figure 672](#XREF_72123__Figure_8__Extended_Message_ID_filter_path30).

Address offset: 0x0080

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

style="font-weight:Bold;">ANFS[1:0]</span>: Accept Non-matching frames standard</p><p class="TableIndent">Defines how received messages with 11-bit IDs that do not match any element of the filter list are treated.</p><p class="TableIndent">00: Accept in Rx FIFO 0</p><p class="TableIndent">01: Accept in Rx FIFO 1</p><p class="TableIndent">10: Reject</p><p class="TableIndent">11: Reject</p><p class="TableIndent">Defines how received messages with 29-bit IDs that do not match any element of the filter list are treated.</p><p class="TableIndent">00: Accept in Rx FIFO 0</p><p class="TableIndent">01: Accept in Rx FIFO 1</p><p class="TableIndent">10: Reject</p><p class="TableIndent">11: Reject</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield is write-protected (P), which means that write access is possible only when the CCE and INIT bits of the FDCAN_CCCR register are both set.</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RRFS</span>: Reject remote frames standard</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Filter remote frames with 11-bit standard IDs</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Reject all remote frames with 11-bit standard IDs</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is write-protected (P), which means that write access is possible only when the CCE and INIT bits of the FDCAN_CCCR register are both set.</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">RRFE</span>: Reject remote frames extended</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Filter remote frames with 29-bit standard IDs</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Reject all remote frames with 29-bit standard IDs</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is write-protected (P), which means that write access is possible only when the CCE and INIT bits of the FDCAN_CCCR register are both set.</p></td></tr></table></div>

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="113.39px"/><col width="501.71px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:29</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="100.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 28:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">EIDM[28:0]</span>: Extended ID mask</p><p class="TableIndent">For acceptance filtering of extended frames the extended ID AND mask is AND-ed with the message ID of a received frame. Intended for masking of 29-bit IDs in SAE J1939. With the reset value of all bits set, the mask is not active.</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield is write-protected (P), which means that write access is possible only when the CCE and INIT bits of the FDCAN_CCCR register are both set.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 44.4.21 FDCAN high-priority message status register (FDCAN\_HPMS)

This register is updated every time a message ID filter element configured to generate a priority event match. This can be used to monitor the status of incoming high priority messages and to enable fast access to these messages.

Address offset: 0x0088

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

When RF0L is cleared, this bit is also cleared.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No Rx FIFO 0 message lost</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Rx FIFO 0 message lost, also set after write attempt to Rx FIFO 0 of size 0</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 24</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">F0F</span>: Rx FIFO 0 full</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Rx FIFO 0 not full</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Rx FIFO 0 full</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 23:18</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 17:16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">F0PI[1:0]</span>: Rx FIFO 0 put index</p><p class="TableIndent">Rx FIFO 0 write index pointer.</p><p class="TableIndent">Range: 0 to 2.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 9:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">F0GI[1:0]</span>: Rx FIFO 0 get index</p><p class="TableIndent">Rx FIFO 0 read index pointer.</p><p class="TableIndent">Range: 0 to 2.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 7:4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 3:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">F0FL[3:0]</span>: Rx FIFO 0 fill level</p><p class="TableIndent">Number of elements stored in Rx FIFO 0.</p><p class="TableIndent">Range: 0 to 3.</p></td></tr></table></div>

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="113.39px"/><col width="500.04px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="84.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 2:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">F0AI[2:0]</span>: Rx FIFO 0 acknowledge index</p><p class="TableIndent">After the host has read a message or a sequence of messages from Rx FIFO 0, it has to write the buffer index of the last element read from Rx FIFO 0 to F0AI[2:0]. This sets the Rx FIFO 0 get index (F0GI[1:0] of FDCAN_RXF0S) to F0AI[2:0] + 1 and updates the FIFO 0 fill level (F0FL[3:0] FDCAN_RXF0S).</p></td></tr></table></div>

When RF1L is cleared, this bit is also cleared.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No Rx FIFO 1 message lost</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Rx FIFO 1 message lost, also set after write attempt to Rx FIFO 1 of size 0</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 24</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">F1F</span>: Rx FIFO 1 full</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Rx FIFO 1 not full</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Rx FIFO 1 full</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 23:18</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 17:16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">F1PI[1:0]</span>: Rx FIFO 1 put index</p><p class="TableIndent">Rx FIFO 1 write index pointer.</p><p class="TableIndent">Range: 0 to 2.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 9:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">F1GI[1:0]</span>: Rx FIFO 1 get index</p><p class="TableIndent">Rx FIFO 1 read index pointer.</p><p class="TableIndent">Range: 0 to 2.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 7:4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 3:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">F1FL[3:0]</span>: Rx FIFO 1 fill level</p><p class="TableIndent">Number of elements stored in Rx FIFO 1.</p><p class="TableIndent">Range: 0 to 3.</p></td></tr></table></div>

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="113.39px"/><col width="500.88px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="84.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 2:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">F1AI[2:0]</span>: Rx FIFO 1 acknowledge index</p><p class="TableIndent">After the host has read a message or a sequence of messages from Rx FIFO 1, it has to write the buffer index of the last element read from Rx FIFO 1 to F1AI[2:0]. This sets the Rx FIFO 1 get index (F1GI[1:0] of FDCAN_RXF1S) to F1AI[2:0] + 1 and updates the FIFO 1 fill level (F1FL[3:0] FDCAN_RXF1S).</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 44.4.26 FDCAN Tx buffer configuration register (FDCAN\_TXBC)

Address offset: 0x00C0

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="113.39px"/><col width="500.88px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:25</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 24</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TFQM</span>: Tx FIFO/queue mode</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Tx FIFO operation</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Tx queue operation.</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is write-protected (P), which means that write access is possible only when the CCE and INIT bits of the FDCAN_CCCR register are both set.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 23:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 44.4.27 FDCAN Tx FIFO/queue status register (FDCAN\_TXFQS)

The Tx FIFO/queue status is related to the pending Tx requests listed in the FDCAN\_TXBRP register. Therefore, the effect of add/cancellation requests can be delayed due to a running Tx scan (FDCAN\_TXBRP not yet updated).

Address offset: 0x00C4

Reset value: 0x0000 0003

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="113.39px"/><col width="503.38px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="337.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 2:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TRP[2:0]</span>: Transmission request pending</p><p class="TableIndent">Each Tx buffer has its own transmission request pending bit. The bits are set via the FDCAN_TXBAR register. The bits are cleared after a requested transmission has completed or has been canceled via the FDCAN_TXBCR register.</p><p class="TableIndent">After the FDCAN_TXBRP bit has been set, a Tx scan is started to check for the pending Tx request with the highest priority (Tx buffer with lowest message ID).</p><p class="TableIndent">A cancellation request resets the corresponding transmission request pending bit of the FDCAN_TXBRP register. In case a transmission has already been started when a cancellation is requested, this is done at the end of the transmission, regardless whether the transmission was successful or not. The cancellation request bits are directly cleared after the corresponding FDCAN_TXBRP bit has been cleared.</p><p class="TableIndent">After a cancellation has been requested, a finished cancellation is signaled via the FDCAN_TXBCF in the following cases:</p><p class="RegTBullet2">–<span style="padding-right:16pt ;">​</span>after successful transmission together with the corresponding TXBTO bit</p><p class="RegTBullet2">–<span style="padding-right:16pt ;">​</span>when the transmission has not yet been started at the point of cancellation</p><p class="RegTBullet2">–<span style="padding-right:16pt ;">​</span>when the transmission has been aborted due to lost arbitration</p><p class="RegTBullet2">–<span style="padding-right:16pt ;">​</span>when an error occurred during frame transmission</p><p class="TableIndent">In DAR mode, all transmissions are automatically canceled if they are not successful. The corresponding FDCAN_TXBCF bit is set for all unsuccessful transmissions.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No transmission request pending</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Transmission request pending </p></td></tr></table></div>


**Note:**

FDCAN\_TXBRP bits set while a Tx scan is in progress are not considered during this particular Tx scan. In case a cancellation is requested for such a Tx buffer, this add request is canceled immediately. The corresponding FDCAN\_TXBRP bit is cleared.

### 44.4.29 FDCAN Tx buffer add request register (FDCAN\_TXBAR)

Address offset: 0x00CC

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="113.39px"/><col width="501.71px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="116.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 2:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">AR[2:0]</span>: Add request</p><p class="TableIndent">Each Tx buffer has its own add request bit. Writing a 1 sets the corresponding add request bit; writing a 0 has no impact. This enables the host to set transmission requests for multiple Tx buffers with one write to FDCAN_TXBAR. When no Tx scan is running, the bits are cleared immediately, else the bits remain set until the Tx scan process has completed.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No transmission request added</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Transmission requested added.</p></td></tr></table></div>


**Note:**

If an add request is applied for a Tx buffer with pending transmission request (corresponding FDCAN\_TXBRP bit already set), the request is ignored.

### 44.4.30 FDCAN Tx buffer cancellation request register (FDCAN\_TXBCR)

Address offset: 0x00D0

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="113.39px"/><col width="501.71px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="117.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 2:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CR[2:0]</span>: Cancellation request</p><p class="TableIndent">Each Tx buffer has its own cancellation request bit. Writing a 1 sets the corresponding CR bit; writing a 0 has no impact.</p><p class="TableIndent">This enables the host to set cancellation requests for multiple Tx buffers with one write to FDCAN_TXBCR. The bits remain set until the corresponding FDCAN_TXBRP bit is cleared.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No cancellation pending</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Cancellation pending</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 44.4.31 FDCAN Tx buffer transmission occurred register (FDCAN\_TXBTO)

Address offset: 0x00D4

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="113.39px"/><col width="499.21px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="101.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 2:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TO[2:0]</span>: Transmission occurred.</p><p class="TableIndent">Each Tx buffer has its own TO bit. The bits are set when the corresponding FDCAN_TXBRP bit is cleared after a successful transmission. The bits are cleared when a new transmission is requested by writing a 1 to the corresponding bit of register FDCAN_TXBAR.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No transmission occurred</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Transmission occurred</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 44.4.32 FDCAN Tx buffer cancellation finished register (FDCAN\_TXBCF)

Address offset: 0x00D8

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="113.39px"/><col width="500.04px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="130.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 2:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CF[2:0]</span>: Cancellation finished</p><p class="TableIndent">Each Tx buffer has its own CF bit. The bits are set when the corresponding FDCAN_TXBRP bit is cleared after a cancellation was requested via FDCAN_TXBCR. In case the corresponding FDCAN_TXBRP bit was not set at the point of cancellation, CF is set immediately. The bits are cleared when a new transmission is requested by writing a 1 to the corresponding bit of the FDCAN_TXBAR register.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No transmit buffer cancellation</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Transmit buffer cancellation finished</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 44.4.33 FDCAN Tx buffer transmission interrupt enable register    (FDCAN\_TXBTIE)

Address offset: 0x00DC

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="113.39px"/><col width="501.71px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:26</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 25</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TEFL</span>: Tx event FIFO element lost</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is a copy of the TEFL interrupt flag of the FDCAN_IR. When TEFL is cleared, this bit is also cleared.</p><p class="TableIndent">0 No Tx event FIFO element lost</p><p class="TableIndent">1 Tx event FIFO element lost, also set after write attempt to Tx event FIFO of size 0.</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 24</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">EFF</span>: Event FIFO full</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Tx event FIFO not full</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Tx event FIFO full</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 23:18</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 17:16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">EFPI[1:0]</span>: Event FIFO put index</p><p class="TableIndent">Tx event FIFO write index pointer.</p><p class="TableIndent">Range: 0 to 3.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 9:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">EFGI[1:0]</span>: Event FIFO get index</p><p class="TableIndent">Tx event FIFO read index pointer.</p><p class="TableIndent">Range: 0 to 3.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 7:3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="56.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 2:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">EFFL[2:0]</span>: Event FIFO fill level</p><p class="TableIndent">Number of elements stored in Tx event FIFO.</p><p class="TableIndent">Range: 0 to 3.</p></td></tr></table></div>

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="113.39px"/><col width="503.38px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="84.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 1:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">EFAI[1:0]</span>: Event FIFO acknowledge index</p><p class="TableIndent">After the host has read an element or a sequence of elements from the Tx event FIFO, it has to write the index of the last element read from Tx event FIFO to EFAI[1:0]. This sets the Tx event FIFO get index (EFGI[1:0] of FDCAN_TXEFS) to EFAI[1:0] + 1 and updates the FIFO 0 fill level (EFFL[2:0] of FDCAN_TXEFS).</p></td></tr></table></div>

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="113.39px"/><col width="502.54px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="413.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 3:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PDIV[3:0]</span>: input clock divider</p><p class="TableIndent">The CAN kernel clock can be divided prior to be used by the CAN subsystem. The rate must be computed using the divider output clock.</p><p class="TableIndent">0000: Divide by 1</p><p class="TableIndent">0001: Divide by 2</p><p class="TableIndent">0010: Divide by 4</p><p class="TableIndent">0011: Divide by 6</p><p class="TableIndent">0100: Divide by 8</p><p class="TableIndent">0101: Divide by 10</p><p class="TableIndent">0110: Divide by 12</p><p class="TableIndent">0111: Divide by 14</p><p class="TableIndent">1000: Divide by 16</p><p class="TableIndent">1001: Divide by 18</p><p class="TableIndent">1010: Divide by 20</p><p class="TableIndent">1011: Divide by 22</p><p class="TableIndent">1100: Divide by 24</p><p class="TableIndent">1101: Divide by 26</p><p class="TableIndent">1110: Divide by 28</p><p class="TableIndent">1111: Divide by 30</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield is write-protected (P): which means that write access is possible only when the CCE bit of the FDCAN_CCCR register is set.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The clock divider is common to all FDCAN instances. Only FDCAN1 instance has FDCAN_CKDIV register, which changes clock divider for all instances.</p><p class="RegTNote_"><span data-conditional="_fdcan2_2_instances,_fdcan2_3_instances">If several FDCAN instances are present, the input clock divider must be modified before configuring the other FDCAN instances. </span></p><p class="Anchor" style="margin-top : 1.00pt;">          </p></td></tr></table></div>
